newsitem.title: USA: Democrats tab Stenholm as US House ag panel leader.
newsitem.headline: Democrats tab Stenholm as US House ag panel leader.

text.p: House Democrats chose Charles Stenholm of Texas on Wednesday as their leader on the Agriculture Committee, aides said.

Stenholm, elected earlier this month to his 10th term as U.S. representative, had a leading role in the drafting of the 1990 farm policy law and fought unsuccessfully to modify this year's "Freedom to Farm" law, which was the most sweeping change in 60 years of federal farm supports.
In an election-week interview, Stenholm said he would not try to alter "Freedom to Farm" but would try to strengthen risk-management tools for farmers.
Stenholm also said he wanted to see more attention to rural economic development.

In 1990, Stenholm was co-author with Kansas Republican Pat Roberts of the so-called triple base plan that made 15 percent of crop acreage ineligible for subsidies but gave farmers more discretion on what they grew on the land.
A deficit hawk during his tenure in Congress, Stenholm, 58, represents a West Texas district and is a third generation farmer.
